# Make the test suite pass

`catalog/` is a small library-catalog package with a test suite under `tests/`.
The suite is currently failing in several places.

Run it:

```
python3 -m unittest
```

Work through the failures and fix the code in `catalog/` until the whole suite
passes. The tests describe the intended behavior — treat them as the
specification and do not modify them.

Done when `python3 -m unittest` reports every test passing.

All 16 tests now pass when I run `python3 -m unittest`. I left the tests alone and changed only code in `catalog/`:

- **`books.py`**: `parse_book` now turns the year into a number, so `age()` works.
- **`factory.py`**: added the missing third sample book, `Book("Emma", "Austen", 1815, 1)`. The tests only check the title, so I picked the author, year and copy count myself.
- **`fees.py`**: the late fee is now days late × 0.25. It was adding the two instead of multiplying.
- **`inventory.py`**: `recent(n)` now returns exactly the last `n` events instead of one too many. I also made it return an empty list when `n` is 0 or less; with the old slicing, `recent(0)` would have returned the whole history.
- **`members.py`**: the borrowing limit is now 5, matching the policy comment above it. It was set to 3.
- **`search.py`**: it was importing `normalize` from a module that doesn't exist; it now imports it from `catalog.text`
